title: Development and validation of an alternative method for ergosterol determination in alder leaves using liquid-liquid extraction and LC-MS/MS after saponification
author: Kusebauch, Bader, et al.
materials: As shown in section ’Sample preparation robustness’, the sample weight can vary between 10 and 100 mg without affecting the accuracy. Regardless of the sample amount, 10 mL methanolic potassium hydroxide solution (8 g/L) were added to each sample. Afterwards, the sample vessels were connected with the condensing vessels and the whole units were heated in a metal block thermostat (TM-130–36 Thermobil, Liebisch, Bielefeld, Germany) for 25 min at 110 °C. Subsequently, the digestion units were allowed to cool to room temperature for 15 min. The condensing vessels were unscrewed and remaining condensate was transferred into the sample vessels. 5 mL ultrapure water and 10 mL cyclohexane were added to each sample vessel with a positive displacement pipette (HandyStep Touch, Brand, Wertheim, Germany). Vessels were then closed with screw-caps and placed in a vertical shaker (1600 MiniG, Spex, Metuchen, USA) for 7.5 min at 1000 rpm followed by centrifugation (Sorvall Lynx 6000, Thermo Scientific, Langenselbold, Germany) at 2000 × g for 2 min. Multiple extraction of study samples demonstrated that a single extraction step with cyclohexane is sufficient to extract > 95 % of total ergosterol content.

steps.title: Assemble digestion units
steps.instruction: Set up the PFA digestion units (sample vessel and condensing vessel with vapor trap) for heat‑reflux extraction as described by BaekDu (AHF analysentechnik, Tübingen, Germany).

steps.title: Prepare validation and blank samples
steps.instruction: Weigh 50 ± 1 mg of homogenized blank leaf material into each 50 mL sample vessel. Spike each with 50 µL internal‑standard stock (0.2 g L⁻¹ 7‑dehydrocholesterol) except for double blanks (no internal standard). For recovery samples add ergosterol to obtain 10 µg g⁻¹ dw (LOQ) by adding 25 µL of a 20 mg L⁻¹ standard solution and 25 µL of a 1 g L⁻¹ stock solution (for 500 µg g⁻¹ dw). Also prepare procedural blanks (no matrix, internal standard only).

substeps.instruction: Weigh 50 ± 1 mg homogenized blank material into each 50 mL vessel.
Add 50 µL internal‑standard stock (0.2 g L⁻¹ 7‑dehydrocholesterol) to all samples except double blanks.
For low‑level recovery samples add 25 µL of 20 mg L⁻¹ ergosterol standard and 25 µL of 1 g L⁻¹ ergosterol stock (final 10 µg g⁻¹ dw).
For high‑level recovery samples add the same volumes of the respective standards to reach 500 µg g⁻¹ dw.
Prepare double blanks (matrix only) and procedural blanks (internal standard only).

steps.title: Saponify and extract ergosterol
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL methanolic KOH (8 g L⁻¹) to each vessel, connect the sample and condensing vessels, heat for 25 min at 110 °C, cool 15 min, return condensate to the sample vessel, then add 5 mL ultrapure water and 10 mL cyclohexane, shake 7.5 min at 1000 rpm, and centrifuge 2 min at 2000 × g. A single cyclohexane extraction recovers >95 % of ergosterol.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL methanolic KOH (8 g L⁻¹) to each sample vessel.
Connect each sample vessel to its condensing vessel.
Place the assembled units in a metal‑block thermostat and heat for 25 min at 110 °C.
Allow the units to cool to room temperature for 15 min.
Unscrew the condensing vessels and transfer all condensate back into the sample vessels.
Add 5 mL ultrapure water and 10 mL cyclohexane to each vessel using a positive‑displacement pipette.
Close vessels with screw caps and place on a vertical shaker for 7.5 min at 1000 rpm.
Centrifuge the vessels for 2 min at 2000 × g.
Note: a single cyclohexane extraction yields >95 % of total ergosterol.

steps.title: Evaporate cyclohexane and reconstitute
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL of the cyclohexane layer to a 2 mL HPLC vial, evaporate with nitrogen at room temperature for ~5 min, re‑dissolve the residue in 1 mL isopropanol, vortex, filter through a 0.20 µm PP syringe filter into an HPLC vial, and store at 4 °C until analysis. If needed, adjust the transferred cyclohexane volume between 50 µL and 400 µL before evaporation.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of the cyclohexane phase into a 2 mL HPLC vial (Macherey‑Nagel).
Evaporate the cyclohexane under a gentle nitrogen stream at room temperature for approximately 5 min.
If a different concentration is required, use 50 µL (for dilution) or up to 400 µL (for concentration) of cyclohexane before evaporation.
Re‑dissolve the dry residue in 1 mL isopropanol.
Vortex the solution with a Minishaker MS1 (IKA).
Filter the solution through a Rotilabo PP41 RC 0.20 µm syringe filter into a clean HPLC vial.
Store the final extract at 4 °C until LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: Configure LC‑MS/MS system
steps.instruction: Set up the 1290 Infinity II HPLC (Agilent) coupled to a QTRAP 6500+ (Sciex) with a ReproSil Gold 120 C18 column (100 mm × 2 mm, 3 µm). Use a flow of 0.4 mL min⁻¹, mobile phase A = water + 0.1 % (v/v) formic acid, mobile phase B = methanol + 0.1 % (v/v) formic acid, and the following gradient: 0 min 20 % B, 1 min 100 % B, 7 min 100 % B, 7.5 min 20 % B, 10 min 20 % B. Inject 10 µL, keep the column at 40 °C, and divert the flow to waste from 0–3 min and 7–10 min.

substeps.instruction: Install the ReproSil Gold 120 C18 column (100 mm × 2 mm, 3 µm).
Set the HPLC flow rate to 0.4 mL min⁻¹.
Prepare mobile phase A: water with 0.1 % (v/v) formic acid.
Prepare mobile phase B: methanol with 0.1 % (v/v) formic acid.
Program the gradient: 0 min 20 % B; 1 min 100 % B; 7 min 100 % B; 7.5 min 20 % B; 10 min 20 % B.
Set the injection volume to 10 µL.
Maintain the column temperature at 40 °C.
Divert the eluate to waste from 0–3 min and from 7–10 min.

steps.title: Set APCI‑MS parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the QTRAP 6500+ for APCI positive MRM mode: ion source temperature 350 °C, nebulizer current 3 µA, curtain gas 35 psi (nitrogen), nebulizer gas 50 psi (air), collision gas set to medium (nitrogen). Use the transitions m/z 379 → 69 for quantification and m/z 379 → 55 and 379 → 41 for confirmation. The dehydrated molecular ion [M+H‑H₂O]⁺ is the precursor.

substeps.instruction: Select APCI ionization in positive mode with MRM detection.
Set ion source temperature to 350 °C.
Set nebulizer current to 3 µA.
Use nitrogen as curtain gas at 35 psi.
Use air as nebulizer gas at 50 psi.
Set collision gas to medium (nitrogen).
Define the quantifier transition: m/z 379 → 69.
Define the qualifier transitions: m/z 379 → 55 and m/z 379 → 41.
Use the dehydrated molecular ion [M+H‑H₂O]⁺ as the precursor ion.
